bills.title: VEH CD-DRIVER'S LICENSE
bills.detail: Amends the Illinois Vehicle Code. Allows an applicant for a driver's license to submit, with the application for a driver's license, documentation confirming an intellectual disability or autism spectrum disorder so such information may be included on the person's driver's license. Provides that any such documentation is confidential. Defines "autism spectrum disorder" and "intellectual disability".

label: Week 34, 2026
recap:
This week's activity, covering August 17 to August 23, 2026, was modest in scale but spread across a mix of themes. There were 9 bill movements and 8 case updates, along with 2 federal documents from the Commerce Department and the Civil Rights Commission. Jurisdictional activity centered on California with 5 items, United States Congress with 3, and Illinois with 1. Among the themes present, government use and transparency and disclosure each accounted for 2 items, while consumer protection and discrimination, elections, employment and hiring, and health care each appeared once. Five bills did not fall under any identified theme.

Overall, the week was fairly quiet, with no single theme or jurisdiction dominating the picture. Activity touched on how agencies use AI internally, disclosure obligations such as California SB1159, hiring practices under Illinois SB2524, and health care applications like California SB1133. Federal-level movement was limited to two documents, and no bill should be understood as having passed, only that some records changed status during this period.

federal.title: Solicitation of Nominations for Membership on the NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB)
federal.detail: The NOAA Science Advisory Board (SAB) is the only Federal Advisory Committee with responsibility to advise the Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere on long- and short-range strategies for research, education and the application of science to resource management and environmental assessment and prediction. NOAA seeks candidates with expertise in areas relevant to its mission, including Federal, State, and local government; social and behavioral sciences; artificial intelligence and machine learning; high performance computing; data management, including open access and accessibility; uncrewed systems; whale research and conservation; aircraft systems and modernization; and economic analysis, including cost-benefit evaluation of observing systems. NOAA also encourages nominations of qualified mid-career scientists and engineers.
